clue.text: Rob makes error, misprinting initial letter

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for error is printed wrongly, so it is swapped for another

parts.note: a blunder is a careless mistake

explanation.surface: A thief gets a typo wrong at the very start of a word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misprinting initial letter' changes the B at the front of BLUNDER to P.
explanation.definitionFit: To plunder is to rob or loot by force, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Keep an eye on river insects

parts.note: the Po is the main river of Italy
lice are small parasitic insects

explanation.surface: Watch out for the bugs living by the river.
explanation.definitionFit: To police an area is to monitor or keep watch over it.

clue.text: Old letter withdrawn, so ignored

indicators.note: the word so is ignored and so left out

parts.note: unsocial means withdrawn, shunning company
taken as written

explanation.surface: An old letter was taken back and so went unread.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncial is an old style of rounded capital script used in early manuscripts.

clue.text: Relegation that's left one in ruin

indicators.note: the letters for left and one are put inside the word for relegation

parts.note: demotion is being moved down, relegation
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A football club's drop to a lower league has left it in ruins.
explanation.definitionFit: Demolition is destruction, the reduction of something to ruin.

clue.text: Forest casualty — endless to-do after game

indicators.note: the second piece comes after the first

parts.note: RU is rugby union

indicators.note: the last letter of the word for to-do is cut off

parts.note: a fuss is a to-do, a commotion

explanation.surface: A death in the woods causes a never-ending stir after a game.
explanation.walkthrough: William II, called Rufus, was killed by an arrow while hunting in the New Forest, an English woodland, in 1100.
explanation.definitionFit: King William Rufus died in a hunting accident in the New Forest, making him its most famous casualty.

clue.text: Illness got rid of, looking roseate

parts.note: flu is a common illness
to shed is to cast off or get rid of

explanation.surface: Someone who has shaken off a bug now looks pink and healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: A flushed face is reddened, which is what roseate, rosy-coloured, describes.

clue.text: Rule-keeper's advice to shoppers in need of discipline?

definitions.meaning: someone who sticks strictly to rules and forms, with 's read as is

definitions.text: advice to shoppers in need of discipline?
definitions.meaning: read as three words, telling shoppers to make a shopping list

explanation.surface: A stickler tells disorganised shoppers how to get their act together.
explanation.definitionFit: A formalist insists on strict observance of rules and conventions.

clue.text: Superior politicians who enforce the rules?

parts.note: U means upper-class, superior
MPs are Members of Parliament

explanation.surface: Senior politicians acting as referees in Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Umpires, called umps for short, enforce rules in games such as baseball and cricket.

clue.text: This person thrown out of home and chucked in gaol is troublemaker

indicators.note: the word for this person is thrown out of the next word

parts.note: me is this person, the setter

indicators.note: the letters are chucked about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone evicted and thrown into jail is a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing ME from HOME leaves HO; 'chucked' rearranges INGAOL to OLIGAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A hooligan is a violent, rowdy young person who makes trouble.

clue.text: Yielded, being put off

definitions.meaning: ... to someone means gave way to them

explanation.definitionFit: Deferring means both submitting to someone and postponing until later.

clue.text: Substitute, inferior, to make an appearance, we hear

indicators.note: says the words for the two ideas are spoken, and the entry is what they sound like

parts.note: inferior is low, and to make an appearance is to come; spoken together they make the entry

explanation.surface: A second-rate stand-in shows up, by all reports.
explanation.definitionFit: A locum is a doctor or cleric standing in for another, so a substitute.

clue.text: Female I reprimand is able to stand the heat

parts.note: a reproof is a rebuke or reprimand

explanation.surface: A woman told off at work proves she can handle the pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: Fireproof things resist burning, so they can withstand heat without damage.

clue.text: Fish served with the French salad — as a rule it's "gassy"

parts.note: char is a fish of the trout family
le is French for the
slaw is short for coleslaw, a cabbage salad

explanation.surface: A fish dish with a side salad, which as a rule leaves you windy.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface jokes about flatulence; the definition is the physics law relating a gas's volume to its temperature.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles's law is a gas law in physics, so a rule about gases.

clue.text: Rank of golfer deemed "great", not "good"

indicators.note: tells us the letter for good is not included and must be dropped

parts.note: Tiger Woods, the famous golfer, whose name also means a great cat

explanation.surface: A great golfer's ranking, not necessarily his goodness.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is a level or row in a hierarchy, so a rank.

clue.text: Pretty sash swirls around in dance

indicators.note: the letters swirl about into a new order

explanation.surface: A girl's pretty sash twirls as she dances.
explanation.definitionFit: A strathspey is a slow Scottish country dance.

clue.text: What can define this? "Stored kit" can, possibly

indicators.note: suggests the letters may be arranged in some other possible order

explanation.surface: A puzzle asking what phrase describes itself, offering the letters of stored kit and a can.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges STOREDKITCAN; the definition says anagrams are the setter's usual tools.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's stock-in-trade is the typical goods or methods they rely on, which is what defines them.

clue.text: Firm cautious about idiot that is certainly no high-flyer

indicators.note: the first word's letters go around the second

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
an ass is a fool
wary means cautious

explanation.surface: A careful company is wary of a fool who is no star performer.
explanation.definitionFit: The cassowary is a large flightless bird, so it never takes to the air.

clue.text: Equine disease is astonishing

definitions.meaning: a nervous illness of horses causing unsteady walking

explanation.definitionFit: Staggers is a horse ailment, and staggering someone means astonishing them.

clue.text: Rum dream dissipating over time

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over the next
the letters break up and scatter into a new order

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A dream fading away with the passing years.
explanation.definitionFit: Demerara is a dark rum from Guyana, named for the river region.

clue.text: Those people by river mouth play

parts.note: them stands for those people
the Ouse is a river in England
trap is slang for mouth

explanation.surface: A group of people beside an estuary is putting on a show.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mousetrap is Agatha Christie's long-running London stage play.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mousetrap is a famous stage play, a whodunnit by Agatha Christie.

clue.text: Writer's hard English

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining the definition to the wordplay

parts.note: stern means hard, severe

explanation.surface: An author's prose is harsh English.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Sterne was the 18th-century novelist who wrote Tristram Shandy.

clue.text: Year immersed in deadly sin became less colourful

indicators.note: the letter for year is put inside the sin

parts.note: greed is one of the seven deadly sins

explanation.surface: A year spent in avarice made someone duller.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that greyed turned grey, losing brightness of colour.

clue.text: Energetic type therefore cycles round

indicators.note: says the letters of the word move round, the front ones going to the back

parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore

explanation.surface: A lively person who, as a result, goes out cycling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycles round' moves ER from the front of ERGO to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A goer is an energetic, lively person who gets on with things.

clue.text: A harem won't excite me?

indicators.note: exciting the letters stirs them up into a new order

explanation.surface: A man unmoved by a sultan's wives wonders about himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excite' stirs up AHAREMWONT; the whole clue is also what such a man might say.
explanation.definitionFit: A misogynist, who dislikes women, would be unmoved by a roomful of them.

clue.text: Beth follows this leading character

definitions.meaning: beth is the second Hebrew letter, so comes after this one
the first letter of an alphabet

explanation.surface: A woman named Beth follows the star of the show.
explanation.definitionFit: Aleph is the first letter of the Hebrew alphabet, followed by beth.

clue.text: Old chemist offering something to put on foot

definitions.meaning: Jesse ..., founder of the ... chain of British pharmacies
footwear covering the foot and ankle

explanation.definitionFit: Boot was the founder of a chemist chain, and a boot is a shoe.

clue.text: See lady having little power to make speech dry up

parts.note: Eva is a woman's name
P is the abbreviation for power
to orate is to make a speech

explanation.surface: A woman with little authority gives a speech that peters out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' just invites the solver to observe the build.
explanation.definitionFit: To evaporate is to turn to vapour and vanish, so a liquid dries up.

clue.text: Person quietly pretentious

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly
arty means affectedly artistic, so pretentious

explanation.surface: A quietly showy individual.
explanation.definitionFit: A party is legal language for a person involved in a contract or case.

clue.text: Knowing about the market, showing quick-wittedness

indicators.note: the first word's letters go around the second

parts.note: sly means knowing or cunning
a mart is a market

explanation.surface: Being canny about the markets shows a sharp mind.
explanation.definitionFit: To act smartly is to act cleverly or briskly, with ready wit.

clue.text: Country bumpkin, getting eg attention of Spooner

indicators.note: Spooner, famous for swapping word starts, signals exchanging initial sounds

parts.note: say means for example, like eg
heed is attention

explanation.surface: A yokel getting the attention of a famous Oxford don.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the first letters of SAY HEED gives HAY SEED.
explanation.definitionFit: Hayseed is North American slang for a rustic, unsophisticated person.
